claims.claim: ⚠️ **These children may deteriorate rapidly or become extremely agitated, aggressive and violent**, and may conceal or deny use because of how parents may respond.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Substance use (abuse)' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Substance_use_abuse/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Response to a drug depends on** the individual (age, size, gender, health, mood), the drug's pharmacology and pharmacokinetics, the dose, the setting, combinations with other substances, and previous experience.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Substance use (abuse)' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Substance_use_abuse/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Where a young person has underlying psychiatric or psychological issues, even small or infrequent use can cause a dramatic response.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Substance use (abuse)' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Substance_use_abuse/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Intoxication signs:** agitation, confusion, disorientation, slurred speech, poor concentration, altered perception, unstable mood or gait, vomiting, diarrhoea, incontinence.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Substance use (abuse)' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Substance_use_abuse/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Exclude medical causes first:** head injury, acute infection, electrolyte imbalance, CVA, hypoglycaemia, psychosis, severe liver disease.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Substance use (abuse)' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Substance_use_abuse/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Take an alcohol and other drug (AOD) history** — what, when and how much today; if the child cannot or will not say, **use collateral sources** (companions, parents, family, guardians).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Substance use (abuse)' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Substance_use_abuse/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Examine for signs of use:** puncture marks, cellulitis, phlebitis, abscesses, rash or irritation around the nostrils or mouth, nasal erosion, rectal damage, dehydration, rapid weight loss.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Substance use (abuse)' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Substance_use_abuse/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Review general functioning and psychosocial circumstances; consult mental health** if background mental health issues are suspected.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Substance use (abuse)' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Substance_use_abuse/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **A simple, quiet, uncluttered room; as few staff as possible; a calm, confident, respectful approach**; speak clearly and slowly and use the child's name.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Substance use (abuse)' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Substance_use_abuse/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Brief, frequent reassurance** helps avoid agitation. ⚠️ **Protect from accidental harm** — do not leave them alone on an unguarded bed, and bring the bed down as near the floor as it goes.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Substance use (abuse)' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Substance_use_abuse/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **For the confused child:** regular reality orientation, a familiar object in view, correct perceptual errors, accompany them to the toilet.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Substance use (abuse)' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Substance_use_abuse/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Aggressive child:** keep space and an easy exit, don't crowd them, keep furniture between you, **work in pairs or call security** if at risk; try to identify and remove the cause of anger.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Substance use (abuse)' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Substance_use_abuse/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **A child refusing treatment and wanting to leave when unsafe:** your duty of care may require you to act — follow Code response procedures and consult senior staff.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Substance use (abuse)' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Substance_use_abuse/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Observe and monitor intoxicated or withdrawing children closely** — they are at risk of medical complications.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Substance use (abuse)' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Substance_use_abuse/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Alcohol withdrawal can start before the blood alcohol reading reaches zero.** Seizures may signal alcohol or benzodiazepine withdrawal, or stimulant intoxication.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Substance use (abuse)' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Substance_use_abuse/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Once an intoxicated child seems stable, reassess for withdrawal** — early recognition and treatment can prevent life-threatening complications.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Substance use (abuse)' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Substance_use_abuse/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Refer to the child's primary health practitioner**, and consider a specialist AOD or mental health service. **If AOD raises concern for future care or safety, consider notifying Child Protective Services.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Substance use (abuse)' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Substance_use_abuse/, retrieved 2026-09-23
